topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the lecturer, outline the scope of the cancer lecture series, and state the key learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Genetic Mutations, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiological Trends
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational causes of cancer, contrasting intrinsic replicative errors and genetic bad luck with environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis and the Burkitt Lymphoma Model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infectious agents contribute to cancer development, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular evidence linking Epstein-Barr virus and malaria to Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens, Metabolic Activation, and DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biochemical mechanisms through which physical and chemical agents—such as UV radiation, aflatoxin, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and aromatic amines—undergo metabolic activation and cause DNA adducts or transversions.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation, Promotion, and Host Tissue Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate between mutational initiators and non-mutagenic tumor promoters such as chronic inflammation and phorbol esters, while examining how host developmental stages and tissue contexts modulate carcinogenic susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity, Testing Mutagens, and Evaluating Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental methods used to determine whether agents are carcinogenic, concluding with practical considerations of exposure dose and risk-benefit evaluation.
